why: Takes the ring off the life counter, restoring the state the stylesheet conceded in a comment for as long as the rule existed: with the vignette cancelled and the scale removed, 'you lost a life' under reduced motion is a hue change on one number. `.hud-lives` is not opted out of the `forced-colors` block, so reduced motion plus forced colours leaves no cue at all -- two accessibility settings combining to remove a signal, which is worse than either alone. Captured in greyscale before this fix, the life-lost digit is pixel-identical to the one at rest.
killedBy: hud.css: no reduced-motion cue is carried by colour alone (issue #924) gives every reduced-motion cue a channel besides hue
hud.css: no reduced-motion cue is carried by colour alone (issue #924) rings the life counter, which is the channel that survives forced colours and greyscale
